articles.headline: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era
articles.description: Manchester City are expected to be found guilty of almost all 115 financial charges against them. It means an era of English soccer is now tarnished with multiple asterisks.
articles.body:
It was one of the Premier League's most iconic moments: May 2014 and Steven Gerrard, Liverpool's heroic captain, finally lifts the Premier League trophy alongside manager Brendan Rodgers, who ended the club's quarter-century wait to become champions of England once again. What a story.

England's fallen giants were back on their perch, and Gerrard, the greatest player never to win a title medal, was able to put the seal on a glorious career with the one major honor missing from his collection. Except it didn't happen. Just like Jose Mourinho winning his fourth Premier League title with Manchester United didn't happen four years later.

Perhaps in a parallel universe Liverpool are listed as 2013-14 Premier League champions and United in 2017-18, but in the real world, Manchester City came out on top on both occasions and on many more. But did they really?

The news that City are expected to be found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges related to breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018 -- neither City nor the Premier League deny the verdict of the independent panel -- means that everything they achieved during that period is now in question. City have consistently denied all the charges and are expected to appeal the verdict.

Forget the asterisks next to those title wins and cup triumphs -- those moments that have been imprinted forever on the fabric of English football. The imprints are still there -- they will never go away -- but neither will the stain and the stench of being found guilty of breaking the rules -- cheating -- to claim their own glorious moments and, just as importantly, deny others from experiencing them.

So next time you see a replay of Sergio Aguero's famous title-winning goal in the final seconds of the 3-2 win against Queen's Park Rangers on the final day of the 2011-12 season, ask yourself whether it is valid. Or more likely, the footage becomes nothing more than the Premier League's version of Ben Johnson sprinting to gold in the 1988 Olympics 100-meter final or any of the seven consecutive Tour de France wins by Lance Armstrong between 1999 and 2005.

Johnson and Armstrong were both unmasked as drug cheats and stripped of their titles. That may yet happen to City when the Premier League rolls out its sanctions for the industrial scale breaches that the club has been found guilty of -- massive fines and points deductions which could lead to relegation are likely -- but the problem is that nobody really remembers who came second in an unfair race.

Who did Armstrong beat into second place in those seven successive wins? Good luck answering that without using Wikipedia. But for those like Gerrard, Rodgers and Mourinho, finishing second to City had its costs and real-life consequences.

Gerrard would retire without ever having won the Premier League, and he has since admitted that his slip in a 2-0 home defeat against Chelsea, which tilted the title race in City's favour, still haunts him every day.

articles.description: Arsenal and Liverpool are upping their interest in Brentford's Kevin Schade, while the rest of Europe chases center backs. Transfer Talk has the latest.

articles.body:
Arsenal and Liverpool have identified Brentford's Kevin Schade as a potential addition to their squads, while the rest of Europe chases new center back options.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- There is increasing interest in Brentford winger Kevin Schade from Arsenal and Liverpool, according to Sky Sports. Brentford have held initial talks with the Germany international about extending his contract to see off that interest, with the aforementioned pair being the most serious about signing the 24-year-old when the summer transfer window drew to a close, although Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur are also admirers. Schade has entered the last two years of his current deal and Brentford are keen to offer him improved terms.

- Inter Milan center back Alessandro Bastoni has re-emerged as a transfer option for Barcelona, while Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester City also retain an interest in him, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old was the topic of serious interest during the summer, but Inter remained firm on their valuation of close to £70 million for the Italy international. Chelsea would benefit from his ability to play in a back three, while Liverpool and City are looking at him as they prepare to eventually lose Virgil van Dijk and Rúben Dias.

- Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City are all keen on a potential deal for versatile Atlético Madrid midfielder Marcos Llorente, whose contract expires in the summer, according to TEAMtalk. Madrid are in talks with the 31-year-old over fresh terms and there is confidence within the Spanish club that an agreement will be reached. The situation has still attracted interest from the Premier League, with the trio of giants assessing whether Llorente could become available.

- Real Madrid are keeping an eye on Stuttgart center back Finn Jeltsch, reports Spanish newspaper AS. Madrid have signed Dean Huijsen and Ibrahima Konaté in the last two summer transfer windows but continue their efforts to strengthen the heart of their defence, and they are now monitoring several players from around the world. Jeltsch, 20, received his first Germany call-up from Jürgen Klopp this international window having joined Stuttgart from Nurnberg in January 2025.

- Liverpool are very satisfied with Ronald Araújo during his loan from Barcelona and could trigger their option to permanently sign the defender for €55 million, reports Spanish outlet Mundo Deportivo. The Uruguay international has played seven matches for the Reds, five of those coming as a starter, but he is already convincing the club and Andoni Iraola. The versatility displayed by the 27-year-old to play both right-back and centre-back has also caught the eye.

articles.headline: Man City charges: Premier League clubs seeking legal advice amid expected guilty verdicts - sources
articles.description: Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice amid an expectation that Man City have been found guilty of hundreds of breaches of financial regulations, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: マンCの違反疑惑：有罪判決の予想を受けプレミアリーグのクラブが法的助言を求める — 情報筋
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNが情報筋から得た情報によると、マンチェスター・シティが数百件におよぶ財務規制違反で有罪とされるとの見込みが高まる中、プレミアリーグの各クラブが法的アドバイスを求めているとのことです。
articles.body:
A number of Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice amid an expectation that Manchester City have been found guilty of hundreds of breaches of financial regulations, sources told ESPN.

The decision of the independent panel that heard the Premier League's case against City has not been formally communicated.

However, a source has told ESPN that they've been made aware that a decision has been reached after deliberations which lasted 22 months.

City are refusing to deny that they've been informed that a guilty verdict has been handed down in the majority of the 115 charges which have formed the Premier League's case. The Premier League refused to comment when approached by ESPN.

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

No sanctions against City have been announced, and sources at the Etihad Stadium have insisted that any guilty verdict will be met with an immediate appeal.

But with a number of Premier League executives now believing hundreds of rules breaches have been proved, sources told ESPN that potential compensation claims from impacted clubs are being considered.

Sources told ESPN that a number of clubs believe they have lost out on substantial revenue because of City's actions, including prize money, sponsorship bonuses and income generated by playing in European competitions.

City have maintained their innocence throughout the case with the Premier League and on Friday issued a statement insisting the process is "ongoing."

The club statement read: "The Premier League process remains ongoing with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

- Rodri 'believes in innocence' of Man City, says success 'deserved'

articles.headline: Rio Ferdinand leads reaction to Man City's 115 breaches case: 'Another Premier League medal'
articles.description: The football world has been reacting to reports that Manchester City are expected to be found guilty of most charges in their legal battle with the Premier League.
articles.headlineJa: 「もう1枚プレミアリーグのメダルが」リオ・ファーディナンド、マンCの115件の違反問題を巡る反応を牽引
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティがプレミアリーグとの法廷闘争において大半の違反行為で有罪となる見込みであるとの報道に対し、サッカー界から様々な反応が寄せられている。
articles.body:
The football world has been reacting to reports that a decision on Manchester City's longstanding legal battle with the Premier League over an alleged 115 breaches of financial regulations may be right around the corner. 

City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League, a source has confirmed to ESPN.

In a statement, City didn't deny the verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said they wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

Friday's reports have given fresh impetus to speculation that City could be in line for a hefty punishment, with some hoping the major honours they won during the period covered by the investigation (2009-2018) could be redistributed to their beaten foes. 

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

David de Gea, who was part of the Manchester United team that finished as runners-up when City racked up 100 points in 2017-18, wrote in a post on X: "So... Let's talk. How many Premier League titles have I won then?"

His former United teammate Rio Ferdinand posted: "Another premier league medal to be added to the cabinet."

Rodri, who left City for Barcelona this summer, said he believes "everything was deserved." Rodri joined City from Atletico Madrid in 2019, one year after the end of the period in which the charges relate.

"When you live daily at that club, all the people that worked hard all these years to have the success we had, Pep, the owners, all the guys who worked on it, they can't take that from us. It's something that isn't paid for with money, it's effort, partnership, standing shoulder to shoulder," he told a news conference ahead of Spain's Nations League match against England.

"We had a lot of success, here at Wembley, and I can tell you that everything was deserved."

Erling Haaland was due to speak to the media on Saturday ahead of Norway's Nations League match against Portugal on Sunday but head coach Stale Solbakken confirmed that, given the news surrounding City and what happened at Rodri's Spain news conference, it would be better for Haaland to avoid fielding questions on the issue. Fredrik Aursnes and Andreas Schjelderup attended instead.

Oasis frontman and City superfan Noel Gallagher, reacted to the news on the Let Me Talk podcast, saying he was "a little surprised when I heard it on the radio. Surprised because only that the club have assured us all along that they vehemently denied any of these charges.

"So it was a bit of a shock to find out that we've been found guilty of all but one. But really overall just quite sad really. Sad for the fans and for the players."

Asked if it changes the context of moments like Sergio Agüero's title-winning goal in 2012, Gallagher added: "Our focus as fans is always on the pitch and we know what we saw -- they won it on the pitch.

"Whatever goes on in the boardroom

articles.headline: Ex-Man City chairman says financial punishment not 'sufficient' if club guilty of Premier League rule breaches
articles.description: Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein believes "money is not sufficient" in terms of a potential punishment for the club being found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules.
articles.headlineJa: 元マンC会長、プレミアリーグ規約違反で有罪となっても金銭的処分では「不十分」と主張
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティの元会長デビッド・バーンスタイン氏は、クラブがプレミアリーグの財務規則違反のほぼすべての罪状で有罪判決を受けた場合、予想される処分において「金銭（罰金）だけでは十分ではない」と考えています。
articles.body:
Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein has said he believes "money is not sufficient" in terms of a potential punishment if the club is found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

A source has confirmed to ESPN that City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

In a statement, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

The charges date back to the 2009-10 season, since which time City have won multiple major trophies.

City are expected to appeal, and Bernstein, who was City chairman between 1998 and 2003, would want to see that process dealt with quickly.

He told Times Radio: "I felt absolutely awful, I felt in shock yesterday, actually. I think you've asked me on the programme because of my time as chair of City and the FA, but basically I'm a fan of Manchester City and have been a fan for 70 years.

"It's really awful that this great period of success, which followed many years of being less successful, when I was chair I think I helped get the club out of a very difficult period and started the road to better things.

"But to see all this tarnished in this way is very sad, I feel particularly bad for the wonderful supporters of the club who've stayed with the club through thick and thin. It's a pretty bad day I think for the fans in blue of Manchester."

Asked what the correct punishment would be, Bernstein said: "First of all, the timing of this I think is crucial. This whole process has taken too long already.

"So the appeal process now has to be done quickly because... You've got the club playing with this cloud over its head and it's just not viable.

"The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, I think that would be a disaster. Not just for this particular case but for English football generally. The timing is crucial.

"I can't give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty.

"All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that."

- Ferdinand leads reaction to Man City's 115 breaches case: 'Another Premier League medal'

- Rodri 'believes in innocence' of Man City, says success 'deserved'

Culture secretary Lisa Nandy described the case as "unsettling" for football fans and hopes for a swift resolution.

She told the BBC: "I think most football fans will be feeling this is not a good moment for football as a whole and I think Manchester City fans will be feeling very anxious about what happens next.

articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Falcons beat the Packers on Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 15 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody gives three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Could the Broncos upset the Rams? Will the Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III and Xavier Worthy score against the Dolphins? Is Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud a fantasy sleeper against the Colts? And could the most entertaining game of the week be ... Raiders-Saints? Let's make 15 big predictions for all of Sunday and Monday's action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Other predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Denver Broncos +2.5 (+114) vs. Los Angeles Rams

Denver has the defensive formula to win this. With wide receiver Puka Nacua likely sidelined (groin), Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II can focus on Davante Adams. Meanwhile, Denver's pass rush can attack a vulnerable Rams offensive line. That pressure could keep Matthew Stafford from finding the rhythm he showed against the Giants.

On the other side of the ball, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix can use quick throws to find wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and avoid long third downs.

Dallas Cowboys +3.5 (+135) vs. Baltimore Ravens

The Cowboys' path is to make Baltimore play from behind in Rio de Janeiro. That shouldn't be hard since the sharpness of QB Dak Prescott and Dallas' passing game gives the team a real chance to score early, putting more pressure on Lamar Jackson and a Ravens offensive line that struggled against New Orleans. The Cowboys' biggest concern is holding up against the Ravens' rushing attack.

Walder predicts three stat lines

Abdul Carter, Edge, New York Giants: 2.0 sacks, 6 pressures, 27% pass rush win rate

Carter's rookie season was noteworthy because, despite just 4.0 sacks, he finished top-10 in pass rush win rate at edge. That was a strong sign about the player he could become, and that signal has persisted in Year 2.

Carter ranks 11th in pass rush win rate at edge and is tied for the fifth-most pass rush wins among all players. In Week 3, Carter gets the chance to run after second-year quarterback Cam Ward, whose 8.8% sack rate since the start of last season ranks third worst among qualifying quarterbacks.

Worthy's production has been lackluster to start the season, but that could easily turn around against the Dolphins. For starters, Worthy is a candidate for some positive regression. articles.headline: Barcelona's start to season is best in Europe's top 5 leagues for almost 100 years
articles.description: Barcelona have begun the season on fire, scoring 36 goals in their first eight matches. How does that compare to the best starts for all time? (Spoiler: Very well.)
articles.headlineJa: バルセロナの今季開幕スタートは、欧州5大リーグにおいて過去約100年で最高の成績
articles.descriptionJa: バルセロナは開幕から絶好調で、最初の8試合で36ゴールを記録しています。歴代最高の開幕スタートと比較するとどうでしょうか？（ネタバレ：極めて良好です。）
articles.body:
LaLiga champions Barcelona have come flying out of the gate this season, with Hansi Flick's freewheeling side picking up where they left off last term and establishing themselves as perhaps the most in-form team on the planet.

Before their campaign was so rudely interrupted by a three-week international break, Barça won their first eight games of the season in all competitions, scoring 36 goals and conceding just eight. That run encompasses seven straight victories in LaLiga and a 5-1 thrashing of Feyenoord in their opening UEFA Champions League fixture.

Just to cement their absurd goal-scoring prowess, the Catalans have somehow managed to hit five goals or more on five separate occasions during those eight games. That is thanks in no small part to the incredible form of winger Raphinha, who has been excelling as a stand-in center forward after his club's summer pursuit of Atlético Madrid striker Julián Álvarez ended in failure.

- Soccer's wildest warmup kits: The good, the bad and the ugly

- Why this international break is longest ever (and that's a good thing)

- 2026 Ballon d'Or: Full men's, women's shortlists, host city, more

The nimble Brazil forward is already well clear at the top of the LaLiga goal-scoring charts with 12 goals from seven games (14 in eight across all competitions) so far. That prolific streak that culminated in back-to-back hat tricks last week, scored in the space of four days in resounding victories over Racing Santander and Sevilla.

After signing off with a "perfect" hat trick (i.e. left foot, right foot, header) against Sevilla, Raphinha can now claim to have made the best goal-scoring start to a season of any Barça player in history. The club captain narrowly pipped the previous record of 13 goals in eight games that was set by Cesar Rodríguez in 1948-49.

Indeed, Raphinha's early scoring form of 12 goals in the first eight LaLiga games of the season has only been bettered once in the 21st century. That was by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored a frankly astounding 16 goals in eight games for Real Madrid at the start of the 2014-15 season.

Raphinha -- who has somehow missed out on being nominated for the Ballon d'Or -- isn't the only Barça player putting up ridiculous numbers this season. The rejuvenated Lamine Yamal has scored eight goals in as many games while laying on an additional six assists across all competitions -- becoming the youngest player in LaLiga history on record to reach (and subsequently surpass) the 50-assist mark in the process.

In short, things are going well right now at Camp Nou.

Barcelona's performances over the opening eight games of the season have given them a hefty early goal difference of plus-28. It certainly looks highly impressive on paper, but how does Barça's flying start to the campaign compare with the best starts ever made across the top strata of European football?

articles.headline: The unshakable bond between Aaron Glenn and Dan Campbell
articles.description: Aaron Glenn and Dan Campbell grew up playing and then coaching in the NFL. When Campbell made Glenn his DC, their bond was sealed.
articles.headlineJa: アーロン・グレンとダン・キャンベルの揺るぎない絆
articles.descriptionJa: アーロン・グレンとダン・キャンベルは、NFLで選手として、そして指導者として共に歩んできました。キャンベルがグレンを守備コーディネーター（DC）に指名したことで、二人の絆は確固たるものとなりました。
articles.body:
The 2005 Dallas Cowboys were an incubator for future NFL head coaches, with six assistants from Bill Parcells' staff and two players from his roster ascending to the highest level of the football coaching profession.

The future coaches included an intense, long-in-the-tooth cornerback who played bigger than his 5-foot-9 frame and a hulking tight end who was biting kneecaps long before he spoke it into the NFL lexicon.

"He was the guy that Bill Parcells used to use to piss somebody off, and there were a number of fights in practice because of him," Aaron Glenn, the corner, said of Dan Campbell, the tight end.

Campbell and Glenn formed a strong bond that season together. They went from teammates in Dallas to assistant coaches with the New Orleans Saints to head coach-defensive coordinator with the Detroit Lions, enduring tough times and moments of sheer joy.

Their relationship was built on a promise by Campbell, who vowed to Glenn that he'd be his defensive coordinator if he ever became a head coach. Campbell did so in 2021 when he took over in Detroit, where the two developed an even closer bond, and doubled down in their first year together, standing by his guy in the 2022 season when it would have been easy to fire him after a rough start.

"One of the greatest days of my life was him getting the [New York Jets] job, and one of the worst days of my life was him getting that job because you know you're losing a little piece of you," Campbell said Friday. "That's what he meant to me and to us. So, that's hard."

On Sunday, they will face each other for the first time as head coaches (both sitting at 1-1), with Glenn bringing the Jets to Ford Field -- his home from 2021 to 2024. And nearly 500 miles away, at his house in Saratoga Springs, New York, the legendary Parcells will watch with pride.

"I always told them all that [coaching] is not for well-adjusted people, so I don't know why they would pick that profession," Parcells said with a hint of sarcasm, alluding to Campbell, Glenn and his many protégés. "But they're football guys. They love it. That's their game."

No change for the better

Campbell knew changes needed to be made in 2022 when the Lions were off to a 1-6 start.

Coming off a 32-27 loss to the Miami Dolphins, Detroit scored on all five of its first-half possessions and entered halftime with a comfortable 10-point lead. But Glenn's defense squandered it, leading to a fifth consecutive loss.

To that point, Glenn's unit was allowing a league-high 32.1 points per game, causing him to face heavy criticism, including calls for the first-time defensive coordinator to be fired.

But Campbell maintained faith in Glenn. And the defense gradually improved, which was instrumental in Detroit winning eight of its final 10 games where it allowed just 20.2 points per game throughout that stretch and narrowly missed the playoffs.

articles.headline: Giants' offense about to 'shift' with Jameis Winston
articles.description: The Giants' offense was starting to take shape with Dart as QB, but now Winston has to take over for the rest of the season.
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツのオフェンス、ジェイミス・ウィンストン起用で「シフト」へ
articles.descriptionJa: ジャイアンツのオフェンスはダートをQBとして形になり始めていましたが、今後はシーズン終了までウィンストンが引き継ぐことになります。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- It was several weeks into training camp for the New York Giants when offensive coordinator Matt Nagy mentioned that only half the team's plays were installed. At the time it seemed disconcerting, but it makes sense considering the Giants eventually practiced and installed close to 300 plays, according to offensive lineman Jon Runyan.

All that extensive work is poised to pay off. The offense greenlit by new coach John Harbaugh isn't only Jaxson Dart-specific. 

"Probably the biggest thing is -- one of the things with this offense when we first got started is we wanted to be able to be prepared to have multiple styles of offense," Nagy said. "And so, if something like this does happen, it doesn't put you in a hole where it changes everything."

The Giants' offense was starting to take shape with Dart as the quarterback before he suffered a knee injury in Week 2 and was placed on IR. His legs and ability to run were a big part of the run game. He had 54 yards in an impressive season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys.

Backup QB Jameis Winston had two rushes for one yard in a Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and that came trying to escape a sack.

"All those plays are plays that we have, that we've been practicing and running, it's just kind of more like a shift maybe over a little bit as opposed to ... maybe a lane change as opposed to changing direction or anything like that," Harbaugh said. "More of a lane change."

The most notable change with Winston at quarterback will be the lack of QB runs. Winston, 32, isn't anywhere near the same threat as a runner as Dart.

The run-pass options are unlikely to be as big a piece of the Giants' offense.

"We did have a lot more Jaxson-driven-type quarterback runs," Runyan said. "It wasn't necessarily something that we were going to major in like we kind of did last year most of the time. So, unfortunately, a lot of that is out. I mean, could be here and there.

"Jameis is a gunslinger, obviously. So we're going to run our offense from a run point how I expect we have been through those two games. From a [quarterback] standpoint, I mean a little bit different. I don't think he's going to get the option to run a lot, but you never know."

Harbaugh has insisted since he arrived that the Giants are going to be a big, physical team. That is what they want to be. They are expected to continue to establish the power run game, try to make it effective and then take shots downfield.

This is where it could work with Winston.

"Well, he can throw it," Harbaugh said. "I mean, he's a big, strong, passing quarterback. He can throw the ball. Everybody that follows football has certainly seen Jameis play, and his strengths are evident. So that's what you build around."

articles.headline: Sources: Warriors, Curry reach 2-year extension worth $116 million

articles.headline: Hornets star Kon Knueppel sidelined with hamstring injury
